finalText:
Migration finished. All 12 remaining application files are now on `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

- `packages/accounts/src/repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js`
- `packages/billing/src/repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js`
- `packages/catalog/src/repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js`
- `packages/orders/src/repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js`
- `packages/support/src/repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js`
- `packages/analytics/src/repo/cohort.js`

Each had the same three call sites (get-by-id, list, update); the conversion is purely positional → object form, no behavior change. All files pass `node --check`. There are no tests in the repo to run.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (lines 9, 13) still calls `db.query`.** Its header says the file is a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade, with local edits silently lost — so patching it there wouldn't survive. That's the last remaining consumer of the old form, and it needs a real decision: upstream the change, wrap the adapter, or shim `query` at the `db` layer. Worth noting `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, so the vendored adapter will break then.

**`cache.query(...)` calls** in the repo files are a different object with a different API and were out of scope.

Since `vendor` still uses it, I also left the deprecated `query` method in place on `lib/db.js` — removing it is the natural follow-up once the adapter question is settled.
